function: CSI feedback: encoder at the UE compresses the angle-delay CSI, decoder at the BS reconstructs it, assisted by uplink-derived covariance information (CNN and Transformer) (p. 1-3).
system: FDD massive MIMO-OFDM: BS ULA with Nt=32 antennas, 1024 subcarriers, single-antenna UE; no RIS; indoor 5.1/5.3 GHz and semi-urban 260/300 MHz bands (p. 2, 4).
method: CNN and Transformer encoder-decoder (CovNet) with a covariance processing network, trained end-to-end by Adam on an MSE loss against the true CSI (p. 3-4).
data_channel: COST 2100 generated datasets: indoor (5.1 GHz uplink, 5.3 GHz downlink) and semi-urban outdoor (260 MHz uplink, 300 MHz downlink); 100,000 training and 20,000 testing samples (p. 4).
test_conditions: Random split of each COST 2100 dataset: 100,000 training, 20,000 testing samples; results per environment and CR; Gaussian noise on covariance and uplink CSI in Fig. 4 (p. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: CsiNet, UpAid-FBnet, DualNet-ABS, TransNet, and a modified CovNet ablation; no classical method compared (p. 4).
metrics: NMSE (dB) in the angle-delay domain at CR 32, 64, 128, and 256; FLOPs; NMSE versus covariance and uplink noise SNR (p. 4-5).
complexity: FLOPs in Table I: CovNet 35.15M at CR 32 versus 35.50M TransNet, 16.97M UpAid-FBnet, 4.63M DualNet-ABS, 3.69M CsiNet (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 4: "We generate two types of channel matrices by COST2100 channel model [18] for training and testing". COST 2100 is a listed standard model.
q2_support: p. 4: "The datasets are randomly divided into training and testing sets". The claimed generalization across environments uses separate indoor and outdoor datasets, each with its own split; p. 5: "we test different levels of errors in terms of signal-to-noise ratio" is a CSI-error sweep.
q3_support: p. 4: "The presented CovNet is compared with CsiNet [9], UpAid-FBnet [12], DualNet-ABS [13], and the SOTA TransNet [10]". All four are learned; classical CS and codebook methods are only named on p. 1 and never compared; the modified CovNet is an ablation.
q4_support: p. 4: "computation complexity measured by floating point operations (FLOPs)". Table I (p. 5) lists FLOPs for CovNet and every compared network at each CR.
q5_support: p. 4: "We generate two types of channel matrices by COST2100 channel model". The authors generated the data; no code or data link and no public dataset is named in the 5 pages.
notes: Area 2 (CSI feedback with covariance side information). q3 fails only because no non-learned baseline is compared; LASSO, BM3D-AMP, and codebook methods appear in the introduction (p. 1) but not in the results. q5: COST 2100 data were self-generated and not released. The PDF is the arXiv:2412.12875v1 preprint (p. 1) and prints no DOI; its title and letter format agree with the DOI.
